title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Work IQ REST API for custom apps, billed in Copilot Credits
summary: Hold for corrections to governance guidance. The service-removal instructions omit the restriction against disabling a policy's last enabled service, and the blanket statement that MCP policies have no documented REST applicability overlooks Microsoft's connector governance documentation.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Setting state to disabled removes a service from a policy, without stating the last-enabled-service restriction.
claims.quote: Setting state to disabled is the removal semantic; the entry is retained in that state, and the collection has no DELETE. Disabling the last enabled service is refused with a 409 atLeastOneServiceRequired response.
claims.fix: Replace 'The request body sets state; disabled removes a service.' in controls[0].note and its rendered copy with 'The request body sets state; disabled removes a service unless it is the policy's last enabled service, which returns 409 atLeastOneServiceRequired.' Add 'The API refuses to disable a policy's last enabled service.' to the At rollout service-exclusion bullet. Keep the documented PATCH call unchanged.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not document applicability of Work IQ MCP policy controls to the REST API.
claims.quote: Work IQ MCP provides Rego-based policy governance to control access to connectors through Work IQ APIs. Connector access is enabled by default. Administrators can explicitly enable or disable connector participation in Work IQ paths through tenant-level policies.
claims.fix: Remove 'Microsoft Learn pages read for this briefing do not apply them to the REST API (see Open questions).' The connector documentation explicitly describes tenant policies controlling connector participation through Work IQ APIs and includes a Work IQ REST API section. Do not replace it with a claim that all MCP controls or the MCP server block govern REST.
